speaker: Doctor
text: I see you have fatigue, abdominal pain, night sweats, weight loss, and enlarged supraclavicular lymph nodes. To narrow this down, have you noticed any changes in your bowel habits, stool color, or appetite recently? Also, do you have any history of recent travel or exposure to tuberculosis?

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling very tired and have had worsening abdominal pain for about four weeks. I have also had drenching night sweats and lost about twelve pounds.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for sharing that. Given your weight loss and night sweats, have you noticed any skin rashes, joint pain, or shortness of breath? Also, do you have a family history of autoimmune diseases or liver conditions?

REQUEST TEST: CBC, Comprehensive Metabolic Panel, LDH, ESR, HIV test.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The elevated white blood cell count and high LDH with normal ESR are concerning; have you noticed any lumps or swelling in your neck, armpits, or groin recently? Additionally, have you been experiencing persistent cough or any difficulty swallowing?

REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal Ultrasound, Chest X-Ray.

speaker: Patient
text: I noticed swelling in my neck over the last few days. It does not hurt, but it feels enlarged and fixed.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Hodgkin Lymphoma. The combination of B-symptoms (fever, night sweats, weight loss), painless supraclavicular lymphadenopathy, elevated LDH, and elevated WBC strongly suggests a lymphoproliferative disorder, likely Hodgkin Lymphoma given the "fixed" nature of the nodes.
